It is not a conformance claim - no clause was audited against this record and no assessment was performed.

safety_class_disclaimer.not_a_project_published_artefact_reason: This requirement belongs to the fictional reference project this corpus declares in its synthetic_reference profile, not to the foxBMS 2 product. foxBMS 2 published no requirement of any kind with an identifier, and nothing was ever allocated to an ASIL on its behalf. It is the reference project's contactor-driver requirement, written by this corpus. Its 30 ms mechanical figure is FB2-ASM-006, a declared assumption of the fictional project.
safety_class_disclaimer.misreading_warning: A reader who sees an ASIL_D hardware requirement with a controlled slew rate and a < 2 ms feedback latency mapped to ISO 26262 Part 5 Clause 7 with status `mapped` will conclude the actuation timing is characterised and verified. The slew rate is a property of a board in a repository this corpus cannot read, the < 2 ms is unsourced, and the budget that appears to close closes on an assumption.

derivation_basis.locator: src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c:125-163 (CONT_CheckFeedback) for the feedback the latency figure is about and src/app/driver/sbc/fs8x_driver/sbc_fs8x.c:160-182 (FS8x_WD_Refresh) for the driver-side watchdog; FB2-SRC-HW-000001 - an Altium .SchDoc in the separate foxBMS2_hw repository, absent here, content_hash 'unresolved'. Pinned commit 308028fb13d046ba29b98886895c2e17937b1437. The 30 ms mechanical opening is FB2-ASM-006, not the source.
derivation_basis.what_it_supports: That the pinned source confirms contactor feedback and supervises the driver, so actuation and feedback are real subjects for a hardware requirement. It supports nothing about the slew rate, the < 2 ms latency, or the ASIL.

revision_history.author: hw_engineer
revision_history.description: Regenerated as a dependent of finding FB2-REV-FND-000024. The rationale cited 'FSR-003 30 ms latency budget', which is the mechanical opening time of FB2-PRM-000005 and not the budget FSR-000003 spends: that requirement's reaction budget is 5 + 30 + 5 = 40 ms from the fault request to feedback-confirmed open. The rationale now states the three segments and the 35 ms mechanically-open and 40 ms feedback-confirmed points. Separately, this record's weld-detection criterion states 100 ms while FB2-SAF-FSR-000003 states 50 ms for the same weld-detection latency; that disagreement is a further cross-record numeric inconsistency of the same class as finding FB2-REV-FND-000024, is NOT resolved here because no record in the corpus settles which of the two is the intended weld-detection budget, and is reported for a decision rather than silently harmonised. The 100 ms figure itself is unchanged; only the measure text now records that the disagreement exists. The coil-slew and feedback-latency criteria and the statement are unchanged.

revision_history.author: corpus_governance
revision_history.description: Added safety_class_disclaimer, carrying no modification of the statement, the ASIL value, the allocation, the acceptance criteria or any standards mapping. The defect corrected is legibility: this record was already marked `profile: synthetic_reference` and, for the SYRs, already says in its own limitations field that it establishes nothing about the real project - but a reader skimming `artifact_type`, `asil` and `standards_mappings` sees a safety requirement at an ASIL with an ISO 26262 clause and status `mapped`, and reads it as an allocated, conformant safety obligation of the product. It is a requirement of the fictional reference project this corpus declares. derivation_basis names what the derivation actually rests on - for most of these, specific pinned file:line ranges, and for FB2-SAF-FSR-000004, FB2-HW-TSR-000004, FB2-SYS-SYR-000004 and FB2-SYS-SYR-000005, the explicit statement that there is no such source because the subject does not exist - and states what it does not support. No other field of the record was modified.

statement: The SBC (FS85xx) shall drive contactor coils with controlled slew rate and monitor auxiliary feedback contacts with < 2 ms latency.
rationale: Contactor control and feedback monitoring must meet the FB2-SAF-FSR-000003 reaction budget: 5 ms coil command plus 30 ms mechanical opening (FB2-PRM-000005) reaches the mechanically open state 35 ms after the fault request, and 5 ms of auxiliary feedback confirmation completes the reaction 40 ms after it

acceptance_criteria.measure: Time from contactor state change to SW notification

Feedback mismatch detection time. The criterion is the weld detection budget of the actuated path and is deliberately not the reaction budget of FB2-SAF-FSR-000003, which is 40 ms end to end; see finding FB2-REV-FND-000024 for the 50 ms figure recorded here and the 100 ms figure of FB2-HW-TSR-000003
